faq.q: My workbook has several sheets — can I convert all of them at once?
faq.a: Yes. Load the workbook and the 'Sheet' dropdown lists every sheet. Convert one with 'Download CSV', or click 'All sheets as ZIP' to get each non-empty sheet as its own CSV inside a single ZIP, plus a README.txt noting the separator, BOM setting and any empty sheets that were skipped.

faq.q: Why does Excel turn my Hindi text or the ₹ sign into question marks, and how do I stop it?
faq.a: Excel reads a plain CSV in your system's regional encoding rather than UTF-8. Keep the 'Excel-friendly (UTF-8 BOM)' checkbox ticked — it prepends a byte-order mark so Excel reads the file as UTF-8 and Devanagari, Marathi, Tamil and the rupee symbol stay intact.

faq.q: Which separators can I choose, and why would I change it?
faq.a: You can pick comma, semicolon, tab or pipe for both directions. Indian and European Excel installs often expect semicolon rather than comma. On the CSV-to-Excel side there's also an 'auto-detect' option that counts candidate separators on the first non-empty line, outside quotes, to guess the right one.

faq.q: Does the CSV-to-Excel direction produce a real .xlsx file?
faq.a: Yes, not a renamed CSV. It uses SheetJS to write a genuine .xlsx that opens cleanly in Excel, Google Sheets or LibreOffice. You can bold the first row as a header and fit column widths to content (capped at 60 characters wide), name the sheet (max 31 chars), and short rows are padded so cells don't shift left.
